messages:
Maya Chen: FYI support escalated — ACME (tenant: acme-prod) missing ~6 hours of audit events in our SIEM (Splunk) between 2025-04-07T02:10Z and 2025-04-07T08:15Z. Customer saw alerts go dark and wants replay + root cause. Ticket #SUP-4821. Anyone on forwarder/export can triage?

Sophie - Support: Customer reported gaps after a scheduled KMS rotation. They say events were being sent then dropped — they also shared SIEM ingest logs showing `http/2 202` for some batches then nothing. :worried:

Devon Patel: On it. First guesses: forwarder consumer lag/backpressure or decrypt errors during rotation. Will check forwarder pod logs and s3 manifests.

Devon Patel: Running quick checks: `kubectl -n audit-forwarder logs deploy/audit-forwarder --since=8h | grep -Ei "error|decrypt|permission|manifest"` and `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-audit-raw/acme-prod/2025/04/07/`

SecurityBot: Alert — forwarder-consumer-lag > 600s for acme-prod at 2025-04-07T03:05Z. Auto-restart triggered for forwarder-3.

Alejandra Ruiz: I see a restart around 03:06Z and repeated `DecryptError: AccessDeniedException` entries in the logs for a handful of object keys. Probable KMS permission window during rotation. Example: `ERROR decrypt key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/xxxx: AccessDenied`

Ian Gomez (oncall): If decrypt failed we should have saved raw objects in S3; forwarding may have marked those manifests as processed and not retried. Need to confirm manifest/offset handling. Can someone grep for manifest entries with zero-size batches or skipped flags?

Devon Patel: Found manifest entries with status `processed` but corresponding S3 prefixes missing retry metadata. Looks like the forwarder marked them done on receipt of 202 from SIEM instead of explicit ack — race during restart. Also noticed a schema mismatch for `tenant_id` vs `tenant` in the manifest v2 parser causing a small parser exception that suppressed retries.

Alejandra Ruiz: Two concrete failure modes: 1) KMS decrypt errors during rotation that caused exceptions, 2) parser mismatch for newer manifests -> tombstoned without backfill. Both line up with the 02:10-08:15 window.

Maya Chen: Action items proposed: 1) Coordinate with Support to notify ACME with ETA (we need time to backfill), 2) Run targeted backfill from raw S3 objects for acme-prod for that window to SIEM (use replay tool), 3) Patch forwarder to not tombstone manifests on parser warnings and add explicit ack from SIEM before marking processed, 4) Add KMS-rotation circuit breaker and pre-rotation smoke test.

Devon Patel: Starting backfill prep — will run dry-run with the replay tool on a small slice: `./tools/replay --tenant acme-prod --start 2025-04-07T02:00Z --end 2025-04-07T09:00Z --dry-run`

Devon Patel: Found ~4.2k raw events in S3 for that window. Dry-run shows mapping ok after applying a small manifest translation (tenant->tenant_id). Planning real backfill in 30m.

Sophie - Support: I’ll message customer with a temporary ETA: backfill start in ~45m, expected completion 3-6h depending on rate limits. Will include note that we’ll share a postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps.

Alejandra Ruiz: Quick ops playbook notes for the writeup: - timeline of KMS rotation job and forwarder restart - list of object keys that hit DecryptError - manifest schema diff and sample problematic manifest - commits to patch (manifest parser tolerant mode + ack change) - test plan for rotation smoke test

Ian Gomez (oncall): Also recommend a short-term mitigation: disable automatic tombstone on parser warnings and enable immediate retry queue for decrypt failures for 24h while we backfill. I’ll flip the flag and monitor. :eyes:

Maya Chen: Thanks all — please add short comments here as steps complete. I'll open the postmortem doc and assign owners.

SecurityBot: Incident tag added: `audit-export-gap-SUP-4821`, priority P2.

Devon Patel: Backfill started at 2025-04-07T10:15Z, initial throughput looks within expected limits. Will post progress updates here.

Sophie - Support: Customer updated to say they see partial events reappearing in Splunk — will keep them posted. :thumbsup:
